explanation: Deuterostomes include Echinoderms and Chordates. All echinoderms are invertebrates, whereas most chordates are vertebrates. Echinoderms are primarily bottom-dwelling marine animals, ranging from 1cm to 2m. They exhibit 5-pointed radial symmetry as adults but are bilaterally symmetrical as larvae. They possess an endoskeleton made of spiny, calcium-rich plates called ossicles, and use a specialized water vascular system for locomotion, feeding, gas exchange, and sensory reception. This group includes sea stars, sea cucumbers, sea urchins, and sand dollars. Invertebrate chordates are deferred to the next lesson.

questions.q: What type of symmetry is shown by echinoderms at different life stages?
opts: Radial as larvae, bilateral as adults
Bilateral as larvae, 5-pointed radial as adults
Asymmetrical as larvae, bilateral as adults
Radial as both larvae and adults
questions.exp: The notes state: '5-pointed radial symmetry as adults (bilateral as larva)'.

questions.q: What is the endoskeleton of echinoderms composed of?
questions.exp: The notes describe the echinoderm skeleton as an 'Endoskeleton of spiny, calcium-rich plates called ossicles'.

questions.q: What is the function of the water vascular system in echinoderms?
opts: To transport blood and glucose to organs
For locomotion, feeding, gas exchange, and sensory reception
To secrete an acidic mucus that dissolves prey cell walls
To pump air into the coelom
questions.exp: The notes state: 'Water vasuclar system for locomotion, feeding, gas exchange, and sensory reception'.
